text.p: The spectacular fall on Wall Street on Friday will ensure the FTSE 100 index will follow suit on Monday, diving down towards support at 4,200, technical analysts said.
It is possible the index could bounce back a little from there to about 4,240 before being knocked down again later in the day, they added.
Most sectors will come under pressure but banks, insurance and utilities will be vulnerable owing to their sensitivity to the interest rate worries that caused the sell-off in the U.S.
By 0722 GMT, the FTSE was indicated down 37.8 at 4,232.9.

The FTSE had been thrown off course on Friday after hitting a brick wall at 4,335, but the carnage on Wall Street -- where the Dow dropped 148.36 points to 6,391.69 -- means that market bulls in the UK will have a tough time trying to defend the 4,200 region on the FTSE, analysts said.
The bears will again be looking for the killer touch and an opportunity to hit the market below that support level at some point thius week, they added.
And the task for the bulls cannot be underestimated because if they conform to type they will lose yet again in the wake of a downtrend of the past few weeks which has not been broken.
